summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Blanchard v. Arkansas Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the adjudication of three sisters as dependent-neglected based on sexual abuse, holding that the juvenile code requires only proof by a preponderance of the evidence and that the child's out-of-court statement could support the finding.
key_cases.relevance: It is the standard Arkansas citation for the burden of proof at the dependency-neglect adjudication.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile code requires proof by a preponderance of the evidence in dependency-neglect proceedings.

key_cases.case_name: Phillips v. Ark. Dep't of Human Servs. & Minor Child
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the adjudication of dependency-neglect based on physical abuse, holding that the circuit court properly weighed the age and size of the child, the location of the injury and the recurrence of bruising in deciding the discipline was not reasonable or moderate.
key_cases.relevance: It is a clear Arkansas Court of Appeals statement of what an adjudication hearing decides and on what proof.
key_cases.quote: The focus of an adjudication hearing is on the child, not the parent.

key_cases.case_name: Jones v. Arkansas Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the termination but held, as a matter of law, that the statutory right to counsel in termination cases includes the right to effective counsel measured by the Strickland standard, while declining to reach the claim because it was not developed below.
key_cases.relevance: From the filing of the dependency-neglect petition forward, an Arkansas parent's counsel rights are statutory under Ark. Code Ann. § 9-27-316 and are broader than the federal Lassiter floor.
key_cases.quote: The right to counsel in termination cases in Arkansas arises not from the Constitution, but from statutory law.

key_cases.case_name: Lassiter v. Department of Social Services of Durham County, North Carolina
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that due process does not automatically require appointed counsel for an indigent parent in every termination proceeding, leaving the question to the trial court in the first instance subject to appellate review.
key_cases.relevance: Lassiter marks the federal minimum at the moment a dependency petition is filed; Arkansas exceeds it by statute (Ark. Code Ann. § 9-27-316), so a family's counsel rights here come from state law, not the Fourteenth Amendment.
key_cases.quote: leave the decision whether due process calls for the appointment of counsel for indigent parents in termination proceedings to be answered in the first instance by the trial court

key_cases.case_name: Linker-Flores v. Arkansas Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: On the merits of the certified question, the court adopted the Anders no-merit-brief procedure for appeals by indigent parents from termination orders, requiring counsel who seeks to withdraw to file a brief discussing any arguably meritorious issue, serve it on the parent, and allow thirty days for pro se points, and it held counsel's pending motion to withdraw premature until such a brief was filed.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms that the statutory right to counsel under Ark. Code Ann. § 9-27-316(h)(1), which attaches when the dependency-neglect petition is filed, carries through to a first appeal and constrains how counsel may exit the case.
key_cases.quote: the Anders procedures shall apply in cases of indigent parent appeals from orders terminating parental rights

state_agency.name: Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of Children and Family Services

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days to make the investigative determination; one 15-day extension permitted (60 days maximum)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the child maltreatment report from the Child Abuse Hotline (9 CAR § 40-324(a))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Ark. Code Ann. § 12-18-616(a)(2): the timing requirement "shall not be considered as a factor to alter the investigative determination in any judicial or administrative proceeding"

content_required: Where to send the hearing request if the determination is true: DHS Office of Appeals and Hearings, P.O. Box 1437, Slot S101, Little Rock, AR 72203-1437, or DHS.Appeals@dhs.arkansas.gov — not the DCFS address at Slot S560 — within 30 days (Ark. Code Ann. § 12-18-706; 9 CAR § 40-1003(b))
